entry.title: Escalating Violence, Displacement, and Access Constraints Mount for Yemen’s Children
entry.summary:
UNITED NATIONS, November 20 (IPS) - Over the past two months, the humanitarian situation in Yemen has deteriorated significantly following the eruption of hostilities between Houthi forces and the Yemeni troops backed by the Saudi-led coalition on September 3. Marked by persistent attacks on key infrastructure and densely populated areas—particularly in Taiz and Lahj—civilians continue to struggle amid heightened insecurity and mass displacement, with children bearing the brunt of the crisis.

entry.title: After the ICJ Verdict, What for Dhaka?
entry.summary:
DHAKA, Bangladesh, November 20 (IPS) - The world’s highest court has delivered a historic legal and moral victory. It does not get any more definitive than this. On 19 November 2026, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State. It is the first time the court has held a state responsible for committing genocide under the 1948 Genocide Convention. By a 9–6 majority, the judges also found that Myanmar failed to prevent and punish genocide. The ICJ has spoken for the Rohingya. The ruling is final, and there is nowhere left to appeal. However, turning this verdict into a safe journey home will take political muscle that the court itself does not have. The international community must act now.

Read the full story, “After the ICJ Verdict, What for Dhaka?”, on globalissues.org →

entry.title: The Future of Surgery in Africa
entry.summary:
LAGOS, Nigeria, November 20 (IPS) - In too many communities across our continent, a baby born with a cleft lip or palate is met with fear instead of a plan. Some families are told the child is cursed. Some mothers are even forced out of their homes. Yet a cleft is one of the most common and treatable conditions in medicine. A safe operation, done early, lets a child eat, speak and grow up with a bright future.
